conviction_note: Evidence is a mix of small, mostly public proxies: European peers (Randstad 22 Jul, Adecco 6 Aug) that spoke after MAN's 16 Jul guide described volumes improving into July and early August, and MAN's own Q4 hiring survey (8 Sep) rose. Against that, BLS temp help was revised down to declines in July and September and Hays reported weak Q1 fees on 12 Oct. Netting these gives impact_sum +1.05, but no single company-level number decides the print, so p_up is only 53. abs_move 10 sits slightly above the 9.24% implied move, because this release carries the first Q4 guide and the last four prints moved +32%, +0.9%, +15% and -6.5%. The scaled +0.6 is smaller than the findings sum because direction is close to a coin flip, not because the move will be small.
bar: Company Q3 guide: diluted EPS $0.96-1.06 (midpoint $1.01), incl. 2c FX headwind and 44% tax rate; organic days-adjusted CC revenue +3% to +7%; total revenue +2% to +6% on Q3-25's $4.63bn (=> ~$4.72-4.91bn, midpoint ~$4.82bn) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000871763/000119312526305399/man-ex99_1.htm, 2026-07-16; https://www.webull.com/news/15237291763917824). Street: EPS $1.01 and revenue $4.85bn per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/node/62129617); another aggregator shows EPS $1.03-1.05 and revenue $4.86bn (https://es.benzinga.com/quote/MAN/earnings-forecasts). Revenue consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint, and the EPS consensus is at or a little above it.
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA, via equibles): 4.43m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 9.5% of shares outstanding, 5.4 days to cover. That is down from 6.75m (14.5%) at 2026-07-15 and 4.76m at 2026-09-15, so shorts have covered since the Q2 squeeze rather than rebuilt (https://equibles.com/stocks/man/short-interest; curvedtrading shows the same series with a one-row offset: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/man/short-interest/). Skew: the baseline 25d skew is null, so there is no directional statement from options. Put/call OI is 0.98, straddle 9.41%, event-implied move 9.24%. Tape: -11.5% over 20 days, -3.0% over 5 days, -18.5% from the 52-week high, +99% from the 52-week low. Sell-side consensus is Hold (6 Hold / 3 Buy) with an average target of $53.63 against spot of $51.28 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MAN/price-target/).

findings.finding: BLS revised US temporary help services employment to -10,000 in July (from +5,200) and +200 in August (from +6,800), and printed -10,900 for September. That is a net decline over Q3, while MAN guided US Q3 growth 'similar to Q2' (US revenue +6.0% in Q2, Manpower US brand +16%). The US is about $714m of MAN's $4.86bn Q2 revenue (~15%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print, where US operating profit rose to $52.8m from $19.7m and US revenue grew 6%, was part of a +32.4% reaction (baseline 2026-07-16). There is no per-segment reaction history.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-02 (BLS September Employment Situation; page 403s to fetch, figures from search snippets of the page)
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since the jobs report, and the stock's -11.5% over 20 days may already hold it. If fully priced, US-centric staffing peers would have de-rated similarly and MAN previews would cite a US miss risk. None found.
findings.independence: Contradicted by the narrower SIA/Bullhorn hours index (+9% YoY week of Sep 26), filed separately. Macro proxy, not company-confirmed. US is ~15% of revenue, so 85% of revenue (Southern Europe ~47%, Northern Europe ~17%, APME ~11%) is unaffected. Size is net of that.

findings.finding: The SIA/Bullhorn Staffing Indicator for the week ending 2026-09-26 shows US staffing hours at an index of 106, +9% YoY, with industrial +15% YoY and a new year-to-date high. That is consistent with MAN's guide of US growth similar to Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same as the BLS finding: US strength was part of the +32% Q2 reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a members-oriented weekly series that wire previews do not carry. Its contradiction with BLS is unresolved in the public record.
findings.independence: Contradicts the broader BLS series above, so it is sized below it. Narrow software-user panel. Same 15%-of-revenue caveat.

findings.finding: Hays Q1 FY27 trading update (12 Oct 2026): net fees -3% like-for-like, with temp/contracting -1%, perm -7%, Germany -6%, UK&I -5%, and September exit -2%. Southern Europe and North America grew in perm. Hays shares fell 7-9% on the day. This is the most recent European staffing read before MAN prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. MAN's 5-day return of -3.0% spans the Hays day.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: MAN fell about 3% over the last 5 days. Hays is perm- and professional-heavy, UK/Germany/ANZ-centric. Its read-through falls on MAN's Northern Europe (~17% of revenue) and Experis, not on the Southern European temp core (~47%), which Hays says grew.
findings.independence: AJ Bell carries the same update with slightly different reported figures (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/hays-shares-slide-5-decline-first-quarter-fees-2-september). Same document.

findings.finding: Randstad, the largest peer, reported Q2 organic revenue +1.9% on 22 Jul 2026, beating a ~1% consensus. It said most markets are now in growth and volumes improved further into July. That is six days after MAN set its Q3 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MAN beat the top of its own Q2 CC revenue guide (5.8% vs 1-5%) and rose 32%. It beat Q1 and the stock moved +0.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty that spoke after MAN's guide. Revenue consensus at $4.85bn sits only ~0.6% above the guide midpoint, so the street has not leaned into the peer's improving-July commentary. If priced, consensus would sit near the top of the guide, as Q2's outcome did.
findings.independence: Adecco (separate document, below) said the same. RTT confirms the date and that Randstad guided Q3 margins only (https://www.rttnews.com/3669170/randstad-q2-results-up-guides-q3-stock-up-7-3.aspx).

findings.finding: Adecco reported Q2 2026 organic revenue +5.6% TDA on 6 Aug 2026 (Adecco GBU +6.6%: Americas +12%, APAC +10%, EMEA ex-France +8%). Management flagged volume momentum continuing into early August, three weeks after MAN guided Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above, MAN's Q2 revenue beat of its own guide coincided with +32%.
findings.why_not_priced: Same as Randstad: the consensus revenue bar ($4.85bn) barely leans above the guide midpoint, despite two large peers describing improving Q3-to-date volumes after MAN spoke. The 'early August' comment comes from the call summary, not the release page.
findings.independence: Randstad (separate document). The early-August momentum point is from https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/adecco-group-q2-revenue-rises-56-amid-market-share-gains via search snippet. Adecco's EBITA missed, so peers' margin conversion was weaker than their revenue.

findings.finding: France temp employment (Prism'emploi) was 681,540 FTE in May 2026, +0.5% YoY, the first positive annual change since December 2022, after -1.1% in April. That is consistent with MAN's France Q3 guide of 'flat to slight growth'. France is $1.18bn, about 24% of Q2 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: France was 0.0% CC in Q2 and the stock still rose 32%. France has not been the swing line recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Lands inside the guide; essentially what the company told the market to expect. No July-September national figure was found.
findings.independence: DARES/DREETS April data showed metropolitan France temp +0.2% YoY (https://grand-est.dreets.gouv.fr/sites/grand-est.dreets.gouv.fr/IMG/pdf/interim_ge_avril26_v2.pdf). Same trend, earlier month.

findings.finding: MAN's own Employment Outlook Survey for Q4 2026 (8 Sep 2026; 39,878 employers) shows a global net employment outlook of +29%, up 2 points QoQ and 6 YoY. Europe & Middle East is +22% (+5 QoQ, +5 YoY), Americas +36% (+11 YoY), US +36%. This is the company's own forward demand read going into its first Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has been the swing line: the Q2 print with a strong Q3 guide went +32%. The April 2025 print (-19%) was a weak-guide reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but it is an intentions survey that previews do not tie to the Q4 guide. The stock fell 11.5% in the following weeks, which is not what an investor base pricing improving Q4 intentions would do.

findings.finding: Short interest is 4.43m shares (~9.5% of shares out, 5.4 days to cover) at 30 Sep, down from 6.75m (14.5%) in mid-July. Shorts have covered rather than rebuilt into this print. A residual ~9.5% short with over 5 days to cover still adds upside convexity to a beat or a firm Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +32% Q2 reaction came with 14.5% short (15 Jul settlement), and the short fell to ~13% and then ~10% after.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning, not information. The squeeze mechanism is smaller than in July because the short has shrunk by a third.

findings.finding: UBS (Joshua Chan, Neutral) raised its MAN target to $56 from $55 on 13 Oct 2026, two days before the print. It is the only rating action since August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In October 2025 UBS cut its target pre-print, flagging the low end of guidance, and the stock fell 6.5% on that print. This year's pre-print note goes the other way, but the size is trivial.
findings.why_not_priced: Visible on aggregators. A $1 raise implies that UBS's preview did not find a miss. The note's content is not available.

outside_window.finding: Randstad Q3 2026 results (aggregators list 21 or 22 Oct) would be the next large European read-through, after the exit window.
The Oct 15 FINRA short interest settlement publishes 26 Oct, after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR since 2026-07-16: only the 10-Q (Aug 7), S-8 POS amendments, an 8-K item 5.02 board appointment (John Gibson of Paychex, effective Sep 1; https://finviz.com/news/380496/manpowergroup-elects-john-b-gibson-jr-to-board-of-directors), Form 3/4 for him, and 13Gs. No asset sale, pre-announcement or financing.
No cause found for the -11.5% 20-day drawdown beyond the Oct 2 BLS temp revisions and Hays on Oct 12. No company-specific news.
Prism'emploi national July and August 2026 barometers, and Assolavoro Italy Jul-Aug 2026: not found/indexed.

EUR/USD: ~1.144 on 16 Jul 2026 (https://www.valutafx.com/history/eur-usd-2026-07-16) and ~1.146 on 21 Sep 2026 (https://www.poundsterlinglive.com/history/USD-EUR-2026). Roughly flat against the guide's FX assumption, so no FX surprise.

Sell-side previews with segment estimates: none found. September 2026 rating actions: none.

baseline_tension: The skew is null, so options give no direction. The slight positive lean from peers after the guide and the company's Q4 survey cuts against the -11.5% 20-day run-up, which the BLS revisions and Hays partly explain. Both pull p_up toward 50, and the lean stays small.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy loses to a broad series): SIA/Bullhorn +0.3 -> +0.15 because it contradicts the official BLS temp series.

Rule 9 (net of the rest of the company): BLS US temp -0.4 -> -0.3 because the US is ~15% of revenue. Hays -0.3 -> -0.25 because its read-through lands on Northern Europe/Experis, not the Southern European core.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): France Prism'emploi +0.1 -> +0.05; it confirms the 'flat to slight growth' guide.
Rule 7 / core table: abs_move 9.5 -> 10 because of the first Q4 guide and hunters' measured understatement. p_up held at 53.
Left standing: Randstad and Adecco (peer prints after the company last spoke, the pattern listed as having worked), MEOS (guidance line), short-interest positioning, UBS target.
